Hi Elena / Acme ops team,

We wanted to notify you that our Hosted API experienced elevated inference latency across a subset of instances in us-west-2 starting at ~08:55 UTC.

Symptoms:
- Increased 95th/99th token latency for text-generation endpoints (average 95th ~1.9s, baseline ~0.4s).
- Request rate remained within expected ranges; errors did not spike significantly.

Impact:
- Your production calls to model 'rwft/gptx-13b' routed through hosted clusters in us-west-2 likely observed slower responses.

What we are doing:
- We routed traffic away from the affected node pool and invoked automatic fallback to a warmed standby pool.
- Investigating root cause with infra and kernel teams; collecting KV cache metrics and kernel selector traces.
- Posting live updates on our status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-06-03-hosted-api-deg

Immediate ETA: We expect normal latency to be restored for most customers within the hour; we'll update you if that changes.

Attachments: latency_graph_20260603.png (95/99 pct latency snapshot), incident_log_snippet_0603.txt (abridged logs).

Apologies for the disruption — I know latency affects your UX. If you prefer, we can schedule a quick call to walk through what we saw and our mitigation steps.

Markus / team,

Quick update for Acme (cc'd):
- Root cause (preliminary): a suboptimal kernel selection path combined with a transient regrowth of KV cache on a subset of hosted instances in us-west-2. That combination increased memory pressure and caused the scheduler to increase serialization between token batches.
- Percent traffic affected: ~18% of Acme's calls were served by the impacted pool between 08:55–09:15 UTC; we routed the remainder immediately to warm standby nodes.
- Errors: 0.8% 5xx spike at the peak, mostly timeouts that auto-retried successfully.

Mitigation already completed:
- We rebalanced traffic and patched the kernel selector to prefer the quantized kernel on instances with high sequence length variance.
- Rolling restart of 6 affected instances completed by 10:05 UTC.

SLA / credits: Operations — per our contract, SLA credits are considered when a customer sees >30 minutes of degraded p99 or repeated sustained p95 breaches across a billing period. This event impacted p95 for ~20 minutes and p99 did not breach the threshold. I recommend offering a goodwill credit and a technical postmortem; finance can advise on exact credit terms.

Attached I've dropped a short latency snapshot and log excerpt for transparency.

— Sean

Hi Elena,

Thanks for your patience; below is a short post-incident summary and next steps. Full postmortem draft is linked.

Summary:
- What happened: Between 08:55–09:15 UTC a subset of hosted nodes in us-west-2 selected a non-optimal kernel path during a spike in variable-length requests which increased memory churn and serialization, raising p95 for affected customers.
- Duration & impact: ~20 minutes where p95 for affected calls was elevated. ~18% of Acme traffic hit the affected pool; errors remained low and automatic retries handled most transient timeouts.
- Root cause: Kernel selector fallback logic favored a float32 path due to a sequence-length histogram edge case when cache regrowth coincided with a scheduler backpressure window.

Actions taken:
- Immediate: Traffic rebalanced, rolling restart of 6 affected instances, patched selector to prefer quantized kernels under cache-regrowth conditions.
- Short-term: Expanded our warm standby pool in us-west-2 and added a safety check to KV cache regrowth hooks.
- Long-term: We will add a model-level fuzz test in CI that simulates regrowth + high seq-length variance to exercise kernel selector logic.

What we will do for Acme:
- Offer a goodwill credit on this month's invoice (operations/finance will follow up with exact amount).
- Share the full postmortem (draft) and a brief 30-min technical review with your SREs if you'd like.

Postmortem draft: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cRedwoodPostmortemDraft
Live status page entry: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-06-03-hosted-api-deg

Attachments: redwood_postmortem_draft_link.txt (link to internal draft).

If you'd like to take the 30-minute review, we have availability tomorrow 14:00–15:00 UTC.

Again, sorry for the disruption — we take reliability seriously and appreciate the chance to make this right.
